conviction_note: The fiscal Q1 numbers are already public: the 10-Q filed 2026-11-16 shows a $13.1m loss and a going-concern flag, and the stock fell 4.8% that day. Tonight's call is the first look at five weeks of Searles Valley operations, on an asset that was running at about -$26m adjusted EBITDA when bought. The company has a self-stated ~$24m year-one capital need and a going-concern flag, the last detailed Searles update fell 17.3%, and recent earnings reactions were -10.7%, +0.5% and about -8%. That gives a mild negative lean (p_up 42) on a large unsigned move (12%). The scaled number (-1.9) is smaller than the findings sum (-3.5) because the stock is already down 39% in 20 days and 56% below where the chair and CEO bought in October, so a reassuring operational update or a debt (rather than equity) facility could reverse it sharply.

findings.finding: The fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter to 2026-09-30) numbers were already filed in the 10-Q on 2026-11-16. Net loss was $13.1m (-$0.32/share) against a -$0.29 placeholder consensus, cash $15.6m (down from $19.5m at 2026-06-30), operating cash burn $3.36m, and management repeats 'substantial doubt' about going concern. Tonight's release therefore adds nothing on the reported quarter; it is a pre-Searles, pre-revenue period.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock closed 2026-11-16 at 1.59 against 1.67 the prior session (-4.8%) as the 10-Q went out (Yahoo chart v8 daily bars). The reported quarter has been pre-released, so this line should be close to fully reflected.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. It is filed because the panel should know the quarter is pre-released and the print carries no surprise on it. If it were not priced, today's tape would sit at the pre-filing 1.67 level rather than 1.57.
findings.independence: None. This is a single primary document. The EDGAR submissions index confirms the 10-Q filing date (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001888654.json).

findings.finding: Funding gap with a going-concern flag. On 2026-10-07 the company put its peak year-one pre-financing capital need at ~$24m, against ~$15m cash plus a $10m bridge from the prior owner (only $7m funded; it and a $1m fee mature 2027-06-28). The 10-Q says additional financing is needed to maintain operations and repay the bridge. The only named plan is an unspecified offtake-backed working-capital debt facility. At $1.57 (~$78m market cap on 49.6m shares) an equity raise around the call would be heavily dilutive, while a debt facility would be a relief.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-10-07 release that first quantified the capital need and the -$26m as-acquired EBITDA run-rate fell 17.3% that day (stocktitan news list; Yahoo bars 3.76 to 3.11). The company did repeated equity raises through fiscal 2026 (Feb-2026 call summary: 'multiple equity offerings, and warrant exercises', https://www.newswire.com/news/5e-advanced-materials-hosts-q2-call-highlights-ferroboron-initiative-federal).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is -39% over 20 days, consistent with dilution fear. Not fully priced because nothing says how or when the gap is closed. A raise announced with the call (common for going-concern microcaps) lands inside the window, while a debt facility would move the stock the other way. If the market had fully priced an equity raise, the 13D holder overhang and today's thin volume would have shown a cleared stock rather than a steady slide. Lesson 4 applied: the money buys working capital and the SAC restart for an acquired, producing plant. The ramp is partly corroborated (82k to 100k st target, repriced contracts), but the going-concern flag and lack of any committed facility keep the sign negative.
findings.independence: The 10-Q (a different document, 2026-11-16) states going-concern doubt and the bridge maturity: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1888654/000119312526463406/feam-20260930.htm

findings.finding: Tonight's call is the first operating data from the Searles Valley assets: five weeks of production, sales, the SAC plant restart and early cost actions. The asset was running at about -$26m annualised adjusted EBITDA when bought. Management has said the full benefit of repricing (+$22m), the cost reset (+$10m) and volume recovery (+$33m) will not come in the current fiscal year, and that the +65% netback depends on 'the timing of contract implementation'. So the first five weeks are likely to show asset-level losses and old-contract pricing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Searles-related disclosure days were mostly sold: 2026-09-15 agreement -5.3%, 2026-09-23 CEO conference -10.2%, 2026-10-07 detail release -17.3%. Only the 2026-10-02 completion day was +20.1% (stocktitan list, Yahoo bars). Earnings-call reactions from confirmed releases: 2026-02-17 amc -10.7% (2.06 to 1.84); 2026-05-12 +0.5% on the following session after a +32% intraday move on the day; Nov-2025 Q1 'declined 8.21% in after-market trading' (search snippet).
findings.why_not_priced: No production or sales number for October exists anywhere. The 10-Q has none and no 8-K was filed after the 2026-10-01 closing (EDGAR submissions). The sign is genuinely open. The stock has already fallen from 3.92 to 1.57, which prices much disappointment, so this is sized small. If the market expected a strong ramp, the stock would not have kept sliding into the call on falling volume.
findings.independence: Management's own framing of the economics is in the 2026-10-07 release (shared with the financing finding but a different line): https://www.newswire.com/news/5e-advanced-materials-provides-additional-details-on-integration-and-expected

findings.finding: Before the 363 sale, the California Air Resources Board petitioned the bankruptcy court to make the buyer assume Searles Valley's ~$76.3m cap-and-trade obligation. The company's own 2026-11-11 release still lists 'environmental and regulatory liabilities from the acquired assets' and 'bankruptcy court sale-order challenges' as key risks, so any update on the call about assumed compliance obligations is a tail risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction on this line; it was never quantified by the company.
findings.why_not_priced: The outcome of CARB's petition is not in any 5E document found. The asset purchase price ($3.4m cash, 8.3m shares, $6.2m note) suggests the obligation was not assumed in full. This is an advocacy-leaning local source, so it is sized small. If the market had priced an assumed $76m liability, the market cap would already sit near or below it, and at ~$78m it nearly does, so this is partly reflected or irrelevant.
findings.independence: The company's own risk language in the 2026-11-11 call release (https://www.newswire.com/news/5e-advanced-materials-to-host-fiscal-first-quarter-2027-earnings-22887471) names environmental liabilities and sale-order challenges, but gives no figure.

baseline_tension: There is no option skew to agree or disagree with. The negative lean agrees with the -39% 20-day run-up and the name's history of selling Searles disclosure days. That agreement suggests much of the negative is already priced, so p_up is held at 42 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside what is pre-released): the 10-Q reported-quarter finding moved from -0.5 to -0.2, since the quarter was filed and traded on 11-16.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question) and lesson 5 (documents beat inference): the funding-gap finding went from -3.0 to -2.0. The money funds an acquired, producing plant's working capital and restart, and the only named plan is a debt facility, so a raise inside the window is an inference. It stays negative because of the going-concern flag and no committed facility.
Lesson 5 (proxy small): retail sentiment went from -0.5 to -0.3 and the CARB advocacy-source finding from -0.5 to -0.3.
Lesson 1 (a fact is not a reaction): insider buys went from +0.5 to +0.3; five-week-old buys at twice today's price do not predict the call's reaction.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the consensus is a single-source placeholder and the company has no guidance, so all sizes are capped small.

Last lesson (untrustworthy history): rebuilt the base rate from confirmed earnings releases (-10.7%, +0.5%, ~-8%) and the 100% realised vol, giving abs_move 12%. The +20.1% acquisition-close day was not used.
p_up moved from 40 to 42 because the negative agrees with a -39% run-up (lesson 3/7, toward 50).
